newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU aerospace body urges probe of Boeing deal.
newsitem.headline: EU aerospace body urges probe of Boeing deal.

text.p: The European aerospace industry called on the European Commission on Thursday to carry a "thorough" analysis of the megamerger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.

The industry, which represents the European Airbus consortium and its partner companies, said the alliance reflected the U.S. government's strategy to lead the market and expressed concerns about a possible spillover of subsidies from the defence to the civil aviation sector.

"The merger will substantially modify the competitive situation between European and U.S. aerospace industries in particular, but not only, in the civil transport aircraft industry," the European Association of Aerospace Industries (AECMA) said in a statement to Reuters.
"This change comes from the U.S. government's determination to lead the global aerospace market which is now focused on one national champion for civil transport aircraft," it added.
As expected, Boeing submitted its $13.3 billion merger with McDonnell to the Commission this week for approval under the European Union's merger rules.
The Commission has about a month to decide whether to clear the deal or, as it is more likely, to start a full probe which could last another four months.
The case is expected to reignite a long-standing dispute over state subsidies paid to the industry on the two sides of the Atlantic.

The EU side points the finger at generously calculated defence contract prices in the United States, of which military jet maker McDonnell has been a prime beneficiary. Boeing could well benefit too through the merger, AECMA said.

"The US government approach of indirect financial support to the aerospace industry through civil and military government contracts will be facilitated by a quantum jump in pooling the primary civil business of Boeing with the primary military busines of McDonnell Douglas," the statement said.

Airbus' partners are Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas. AECMA represents the industry in the European Union. Its chairman is also BAe's chairman, Richard Evans. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
